cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities that allow attackers to bypass authentication or authorization by exploiting missing validation checks, timing side-channels, insecure cryptographic operations, and session management flaws. The issues include failure to verify user existence, token validity, claim correctness, and the use of non-constant-time comparisons, weak PRNGs, and untrusted algorithm handling.
guideline_text: Trace externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers into privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access. Report code paths where caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 9 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect.

mechanism.missing_guard: caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins
mechanism.name: missing authentication before privileged action
mechanism.sink_shape: privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access
mechanism.source_shape: externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers
mechanism.typical_fix: require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Invalidate the old session and create a new session upon successful authentication.
sub_patterns.name: Session fixation
sub_patterns.root_cause: Reusing the existing HTTP session after authentication without invalidation, allowing an attacker to fixate a session ID.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add explicit validation checks for each missing condition, correct logical errors (e.g., OR→AND), and invalidate one-time tokens after use.
sub_patterns.name: Missing validation in authentication/authorization flows
sub_patterns.root_cause: Authentication or authorization code omits necessary checks on user identity (existence, active flag, roles), token presence, token claims (expiration, audience, scopes), or session state (captcha reuse, realm configuration).

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Set security flags at the correct initialization phase, catch exceptions gracefully, and use framework methods that ensure attributes are applied.
sub_patterns.name: Session cookie security attributes not properly set
sub_patterns.root_cause: Failure to set the secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite flags on session cookies due to silent exceptions or missing configuration.

sub_patterns.name: Authentication bypass and token validation flaws
